ops.title: Review plan: declarative filesystem search guard and authoring guidance
ops.body:
Context: Claude session 618681cf-ba49-452b-8d4f-01e59df55a57 launched overlapping find / daemonkit directory searches during a captain-hook dispatch-stall dependency lookup. Both finds (534, 40736) were terminated. Existing general guard returned None for both exact commands because directory searches and redirects do not fit its rewrite path. The uncommitted draft is not installed.

Review #1, verbatim: "this is super hacky and manual, use the nice abstactions, or add to them if you need to to make this very clear and dclerative"
Review #2, verbatim: "and alos upodate the skill or whatever docs lead you to do this so messily"

Approach after user approval:
1. Extend the shared command abstractions, reusing Cmd.calls, Call, Target and parser token provenance. Expose typed find search roots and traversal depth. Find root/expression separation belongs in the command parser/spec layer; do not move the draft's hand parser into another class or use generic Call.targets, which misclassifies find src -name /.
2. Express broad-root and shallow-depth policy through reusable conditions. Replace filesystem.py helpers with one declarative PreToolUse registration and inline regression cases. Keep shell/home/path interpretation in the shared abstractions. Test interaction with the existing general rewrite.
3. Update canonical captain_hook/skills/authoring-hooks/SKILL.md and its API/pitfalls references: structural abstractions first; extend a missing shared primitive before authoring hook-local argv logic; reserve regexes for textual rules. Add an executable example, not wording-matching tests. Edit canonical sources, not installed caches.

Pitfalls: distinguish root operands from find expression arguments; preserve quoted literals versus expansions and cwd/nested-shell semantics; a pipeline/head or hidden stderr does not bound traversal; explicit shallow depth must be typed and attached to its find invocation.

Schedule: shared API/tests first; hook and skill changes can run in parallel once consuming the agreed API; integrated tests and documentation checks gate completion. Work stays in isolated branch/worktrees; no publishing or live installation yet.

Verification: shared command and condition tests; exact two offending commands; benign find src -name /; scoped roots; wrappers/nested shells/cd; redirects and pipelines; shallow depths; repeated occurrence; combined general/performance dispatch. Run uv run capt-hook --hooks captain_hook/builtin_packs/performance/hooks test; uv run pytest tests/test_cmd.py tests/test_conditions.py tests/test_packs.py tests/test_skill_docs.py tests/test_skills.py; uv build; slop-cop check individually for each edited Markdown file. Public API changes also require the repository's documented gd-build verification.

Mappings: #1 filesystem.py:broad_find -> shared primitives and declarative hook; #2 authoring-hooks/SKILL.md:82 and references -> structural-first guidance and executable example. Await approval under the user's AGENTS.md code-review-response rule before implementation.
